blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The biodiversity hotspot concept was originally proposed by Norman Myers in 1988.
To be designated a hotspot, a region must contain at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species.
A region must have lost at least 70% of its original natural habitat to qualify.
India shares four global biodiversity hotspots: Western Ghats, Himalaya, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
